summary: Over the last 4 weeks, training volume has been notably low and inconsistent, with only 10 sessions recorded across swimming, cycling, and no running whatsoever — a concern with a Half Oceanman 5km swim 14 days away and a 10K run 22 days away. Swimming pace in open water has been sitting around 28–31 min/km, which is significantly slower than the 2:30/100m race target, and the recent 63-minute 2km swim on Sep 19 at avg HR 151 bpm shows meaningful cardiovascular effort at that pace. Sleep quality is chronically poor (many nights under 5–6 hours) and body battery has been regularly low, suggesting recovery is the primary limiter right now rather than training load.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — with the Half Oceanman 14 days out and consistently low body battery (frequently below 50), inadequate sleep is directly impairing recovery and race readiness more than any single training session can fix.

For the Half Oceanman swim target of 2:30/100m, your recent open water pace of ~29–31 min/km (approx 2:54–3:06/100m) is 20–35 seconds per 100m off target — squeeze in one focused pool session before race week to practise controlled pacing at or near 2:30/100m rather than going by feel.

There is zero running in the last 4 weeks, which is risky with a 10K race only 22 days away — keep the Sep 20 long run as prescribed (10–12 km easy) and ensure the Sep 22 maintenance run actually happens to maintain run-leg neuromuscular readiness.

The Sep 26 planned 120km long ride (Wk14) sits only 6 days before race week for the Half Oceanman — cap it at 75–80km or 150 minutes maximum to avoid carrying pre-race leg fatigue into the swim taper.

Avoid the Wk14 Thursday threshold cycling intervals (5x5min at 210–244W) given that race week begins immediately after — this is high-intensity work too close to the Half Oceanman; replace with a shorter Z2 spin to stay sharp without generating fatigue.

proposed_changes.current_session: Pool Swim: min 2,000m, technique drills and aerobic sets, pace ≤2:30/100m
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Pool Swim: 2,000m with specific pacing focus — 6x200m at 2:30/100m target pace with 20s rest, bookended by 200m warm-up and 200m cool-down. Log splits to gauge race readiness.
proposed_changes.reason: Open water swim pace has been 28–31 min/km (~2:50–3:06/100m) over the last 4 weeks, well off the 2:30/100m race target 14 days out — a structured pace session will give the athlete concrete feedback and build confidence before taper.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Evening: 5x5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold), 3min Z1 recovery, 60–75min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with 50min Z2 endurance spin at 128–160W, flat and steady — no intervals.
proposed_changes.reason: High-intensity threshold intervals 8 days before the Half Oceanman risk generating residual fatigue that undermines race-day performance, especially given the athlete's chronically low body battery and poor sleep patterns.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk14 Long Ride: 120km @ 128–177W, up to 240 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap at 80km or 150 minutes at 128–160W (Z2 only, no Z3 tempo blocks) — ride easy and finish feeling fresh.
proposed_changes.reason: A 120km, 4-hour ride only 6 days before the Half Oceanman swim race is excessive and risks carrying fatigue and soreness directly into race week, particularly given the athlete's already low recovery reserves.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Shorten to 14–15km @ 6:45–7:00/km, easy effort only, cap at 90 minutes — no negative-split push.
proposed_changes.reason: With zero running in the past 4 weeks and the Half Oceanman only 5 days after this session, a full 21km long run would leave the athlete fatigued going into race week without providing meaningful fitness gains in such a short window.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with a very easy 20–25 min shakeout jog at 7:00+/km — this is the day after the Half Oceanman race; full recovery is the priority.
proposed_changes.reason: Scheduling a 21.5km long run the day after racing a 5,000m open water swim event will compromise recovery and risks injury, especially with the Treviso 10K only 6 days later.
